# Create and manage add-on definitions

This page describes how to create, edit, and delete Terraform Developer Portal add-on definitions. Platform engineers often perform these tasks. Refer to [Add-ons](/hcp/docs/waypoint/concepts/add-ons) for additional information.

## Overview

The following steps describe the procedure for creating add-on definitions:

1. For each add-on you want to create, define a no-code module in HCP Terraform that specifies a common infrastructure pattern. 
1. Use the Terraform Developer Portal UI to create the add-on.

After creating an add-on, application developers can begin installing it to add additional capabilities to their applications.  

## Prerequisites

To create an add-on, you must meet the following requirements: 

- An HCP Terraform Standard edition account with permission to create workspaces. Refer to [HCP Terraform pricing](https://www.hashicorp.com/en/pricing?tab=terraform) for more details. 
- A Terraform no-code module in your organization's private module registry. For information on how to create no-code modes, refer to the [Design no-code ready modules](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cloud-docs/workspaces/no-code-provisioning/module-design) documentation 


## Create a no-code module

To create an add-on definition, you first need to create a no-code module that captures the common infrastructure pattern. Refer to [Designing No-Code Ready Modules](/terraform/cloud-docs/no-code-provisioning/module-design) for instructions on how to create no-code modules.

You can reference the following variables in the module as Terraform Developer Portal defines the values when the application developer uses the add-on.

- `waypoint_add_on`: References the name of the add-on.
- `waypoint_add_on_definition`: References the name of the add-on definition used to create the add-on.
- `waypoint_application`: References the name of the application for which the add-on is being installed onto by the app developer.

Refer to [Input Variables](/terraform/language/values/variables) for instructions on how to define variables in Terraform.

You may need to create global variable sets within your HCP Terraform organization so your no-code modules can authenticate and interact with your cloud provider. 

You can use the variable to label infrastructure resources in the no-code module so you can associate them with the Terraform Developer Portal application.

## Create an add-on definition

After creating the no-code module, complete the following steps in the Terraform Developer Portal UI:

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/) and select the organization where you want to create your add-on. 
1. In the navigation menu, click **Developer Portal**. 
1. Click **Add-ons** in the sidebar, then click **New Add-on**. 
1. Specify a unique identifier for the add-on in the **Name** field. 
1. Choose a no-code module to use as the source for the add-on from the **Base module** menu. No-code modules published in your organization's private registry appear in the menu. 
1. Provide values for the input variables of the no-code module. Optionally, you can enable the **User can configure this variable when creating an add-on** checkbox to let users provide a value when they deploy the add-on. 
1. Optionally, configure the execution mode that HCP Terraform uses to perform Terraform operations. By default, add-ons use the organization’s default execution mode. You can override the default by disabling **Use Terraform organization's default mode** and choosing one of the following options: 
    - **Remote**: Run Terraform operations in HCP Terraform's infrastructure. 
    - **Agent**: Use a self-managed agent pool. Refer to [Manage Agent Pools](/terraform/cloud-docs/agents/agent-pools) to learn how to create and manage agent pools. 
1. Click **Continue**. 
1. Add a short description of the add-on in the **Summary** field. This field can be up to 110 characters. HCP Terraform presents the description when users deploy the add-on. 
1. Specify instructions for application developers on how to use the add-on in the **Developer Instructions** field. This field supports markdown. Optionally, click **Update from module's README** to automatically populate this field with the value of the no-code module's README file. HCP Terraform exposes the following variables so you can reference them in the developer instructions. 
    - `{{ .AddonName }}`: Populates the name of the add-on in the instructions. 
1. Click **Save**. 

## Edit an add-on definition

Modifying an add-on does not affect existing installations or supporting infrastructure created by the add-on. These changes only apply to new add-on installations.

To edit an add-on definition, complete the following steps:

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/) and select the organization where you want to edit your add-on definition.
1. In the navigation menu, click **Developer Portal**. 
1. Click **Add-ons** in the sidebar, then click on the add-on definition you want to modify. 
1. Click the **Manage** menu, then select either **Edit add-on** Add-on or **Edit inputs**. 
1. Update the desired fields. 
1. Click **Save**. 

## Delete an add-on definition

Deleting an add-on does not delete the supporting infrastructure that was created with Terraform by the add-on. To do so, you must uninstall the add-on from a application or delete the Terraform resources and the HCP Terraform workspace associated with the Terraform Developer Portal add-on. Refer to [Uninstall an add-on](#uninstall-an-add-on) for instructions.

To delete an add-on definition, complete the following steps:

1. Sign in to [HCP Terraform](https://app.terraform.io/) and select the organization where you want to delete your add-on definition.
1. In the navigation menu, click **Developer Portal**.
1. Click **Add-ons** in the sidebar, then click on the add-on definition you want to delete. 
1. Click the **Manage** menu, then choose **Delete**. 
1. In the **Delete add-on** dialog, enter "delete" and then click **Delete add-on**.
